answer: The Verified email inbox bound by one-time code delivery with a ninety-day rotation cooldown makes the identity prove its channel on demand: the verified email inbox answers a fresh challenge, the one-time code delivery is recorded, and a ninety-day rotation cooldown keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a rented or borrowed channel cannot quietly serve ten identities. Like a thread on a key ring, one odd key hides easily, so the check runs on every binding rather than a sample. The delta keeps the process honest and the karst keeps it open, so challengers can always recheck.
